overview: The Council called for the immediate reinstatement of the Veterans Services Officer and requested reports on citywide anti-racism programming following the vandalism of a local art installation. Members also addressed infrastructure concerns regarding curbing materials on Vernon Street and the disrepair of a city-owned property.

items.title: Tabled Business
items.summary: Tabled item 21-545 at the request of the petitioners.

items.title: License Approval: Shari and Grill
items.summary: Approved a common victualler license for Shari and Grill located at 321A Boston Avenue.

items.title: Vernon Street Curbing and Paving
items.summary: Requested a report from the City Engineer regarding why concrete curbing was used instead of granite on Vernon Street and recommended that paving stop until the material discrepancy is resolved. The council further inquired about design specification changes and contractual price differences between the approved work and the current materials.

items.title: Tabled Resolutions
items.summary: Tabled several resolutions in the absence of the sponsoring councilor.

items.title: Reinstatement of Michael Durham
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the administration immediately reinstate Veterans Services Officer Michael Durham to his position. Discussion focused on the lack of coverage in the veterans office, allegations of retaliation against a whistleblower, and the administration's requirement for a specific psychological evaluation.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Retirements
items.summary: Approved resolutions recognizing Dr. Edward Butler on his retirement, thanking Police Officer Paul McGillivray for 25 years of service, wishing happy birthday to Larry Lepore, and honoring retiring Board of Registrar Voters members General Richard Lasky and Judith Murray.

items.title: Vandalism of 'Textbook Behavior' Art Installation
items.summary: Congratulated artist Julianne Otis on her city-funded art installation while discussing the repeated vandalism of the work and the perceived lack of support from city commissions and the administration. The artist detailed the process of obtaining permits and the subsequent resistance faced after the artwork was defaced.

items.title: Report on Anti-Racism Efforts and Social Justice Roadmap
items.summary: Requested that the administration report on anti-racism efforts and trainings conducted under the Social Justice Roadmap, including future funding plans and the status of the Diversity Director position vacancy. Members expressed concern that the role of Diversity Director has been marginalized and remains unposted following budget deliberations.

items.title: Property Update: 15 Maple Park Avenue
items.summary: Requested an update on the future plans and maintenance schedule for the city-owned property at 15 Maple Park Avenue, citing significant disrepair and rodent issues. The discussion noted that previous plans to convert the building into an art center have shifted as other potential locations are explored.

items.title: Meeting Records and Adjournment
items.summary: Approved the meeting records from August 17, 2021, and tabled the records from September 21, 2021.
